title: Evals runner plugins and CI checklist
content:
Quick context and intent:

This is a compact implementation note for the evals harness runner plugins + CI wiring that I sketched while pairing with Marco and Renee. Goal: practical checklist and implementation patterns we can borrow for model onboarding pipelines (fast smoke checks on PR, nightly full-eval, and gated promotion). This is intentionally pragmatic — contains examples of file layouts, required script responsibilities, deterministic seeding rules, and CI recipe fragments (GH Actions oriented) that we can paste into new model-onboard repos.

High-level design principles (short):
- Minimal slowness on PRs: PR checks run a ~100-case smoke set across deterministic sampling of prompt groups.
- Reproducible full runs: nightly or pre-release runs use fixed prompt-set commits and seed values and produce artifact bundles (jsonl + metrics).
- Small surface area for loader authors: a loader interface that supports streaming and a validation shim so people can iterate quickly.
- Keep scoring functions pure (no external network calls) and small, so we can unit-test them and run them locally in CI.
- Artifacts in CI are JSON + plain CSV summaries (no binary formats).

Suggested repo layout (concrete):
- /prompt-sets/ (jsonl per prompt family; filename includes version e.g. classification-v1.jsonl)
- /loaders/ (python loaders, one per dataset family; each exposes `iter_examples(seed, limit)` and `validate(path)`)
- /scorers/ (small python modules implementing Score classes: exact_match, token_f1, embedding_sim)
- /runners/ (lightweight runner that wires model client to scorers and outputs case-level traces)
- /ci/ (helper scripts used by GH Actions: run_smoke.py, run_full.py, collect_artifacts.py)
- /tests/ (unit tests for loaders and scorers)
- .github/workflows/ (smoke.yml, nightly-full.yml)

Example minimal loader interface (pattern):
- function: iter_examples(seed:int=0, limit:Optional[int]=None) -> yields dicts {"id": str, "prompt": str, "gold": any, "meta": {...}}
- function: validate(path) -> list of issues (empty means ok)

Notes:
- Loaders must be streaming (yield) to allow huge prompt-sets in nightly runs.
- Loaders accept seed and should implement deterministic sampling via numpy.random.default_rng(seed) so PR smoke samples are reproducible.
- For multi-shot prompts, loader attaches meta["shots"] = [list of in-context examples] and runner must merge them without truncation.

Prompt-set format rules (jsonl):
- Each line: {"id": "short-id", "split": "smoke|dev|gold", "prompt": "...", "gold": ..., "tags": ["intent:xxx", "format:json"], "notes": "optional"}
- Keep prompt text short when used for smoke; long form prompts ok in nightly.
- Version prompt-sets by filename and keep a small manifest file `prompt-manifest.json` with fields: {"name":..., "version":..., "sha":...} — we store the manifest artifact with eval results.

Scoring functions to include (priority order):
- exact_match_text: canonicalize whitespace and punctuation, case-fold when appropriate.
- token_f1 (for short generation tasks): whitespace + simple tokenizer split on whitespace/punct.
- sequence_lcs (longer responses): normalized LCS ratio to detect partial hits.
- normalized_embedding_sim: compute embedding for gold and predicted, cosine similarity with a threshold; used mostly for semantic retrieval tests.
- structured_field_check: for JSON output, validate presence/absence and exact values for required keys.
- safety_flag_counter: a lightweight heuristic score that just counts hits of blocklist tokens; return counts per case so human reviewers can inspect.

Scorer implementation notes:
- Each scorer is a small class with methods: score_case(predicted, gold, meta)-> {"score": float, "details": {..}}.
- Scorers must be deterministic and side-effect free.
- Provide unit tests with edge cases: empty strings, long strings, unicode normalization, and different whitespace patterns.

Regression detection and statistical rules (short):
- For PR smoke (n ~ 100), we do delta checks: if a metric drops by >5% absolute or relative depending on metric family -> fail the PR. Tune per-metric thresholds in a metrics-config.yml.
- For nightly/full (n > 1000), run bootstrap confidence intervals and compute p-values for differences vs baseline commit using paired-sample bootstrap on per-case scores. If p < 0.01 and mean delta exceeds configured min_effect -> flag regression.
- Always produce full artifact bundle with per-case scores so humans can inspect bromelines causing flips.

CI wiring sketches (GitHub Actions patterns):
1) PR smoke workflow (fast):
- triggers: pull_request
- steps: checkout, setup-python, restore-cache (pip wheel cache + model-client wheel), run `python ci/run_smoke.py --seed ${{ github.sha|hashint }}`
- run_smoke.py: picks smoke prompt-sets (split==smoke), samples deterministic 100-case subset, invokes the runner with model config pointing at the PR branch model spec (or a test stub client), writes artifacts to `artifacts/smoke/${{github.sha}}/` and uploads artifact.
- failure logic: parse metrics summary JSON, fail if any configured gate fails.

2) Nightly full workflow (scheduled):
- runs on cron (02:00 UTC), on a runner with GPU or on Redwood staging endpoints.
- steps: checkout, setup, cache prompt-sets (persisted), run `python ci/run_full.py --manifest prompt-manifest.json --out artifacts/full/$(date)`
- artifacts: per-case jsonl, aggregate metrics, plots (svg) of trend lines.

Caching and artifacts:
- Cache neural-context embeddings or precomputed metadata (use S3 paths) to avoid recomputing embeddings in full every night.
- Always upload artifacts with stable names that include prompt-manifest sha + model commit sha so we can join metrics across runs.

Promoting models (gating):
- Use the metrics-config.yml gating rules: requires that all primary metrics maintain within allowed deltas and no safety regressions.
- When promoting, the release script `ci/collect_artifacts.py` creates a short release note (markdown) describing key deltas and links to artifacts, and posts to the release PR as a comment.

Operational considerations and edge cases:
- Non-deterministic sampling: if a loader depends on external APIs to construct prompts (bad), lock it down or snapshot the generated prompts into prompt-sets before running CI.
- Model nondeterminism: set sampling parameters for smoke runs to low temperature / greedy decoding where possible to reduce flakiness in PR checks. Nightly runs can test with sampling settings the real app uses.
- Long-running full evals should be sharded by prompt family and run in parallel; provide a `--shard-index` and `--shard-count` for run_full.py.
- If the model responds slowly, runner should time out per-case (default 20s) and mark the case as timeout in artifacts (timeout_count reported in metrics).

Debugging tips (quick):
- Reproduce locally: `python -m venv .venv && pip install -e .[test] && python ci/run_smoke.py --seed 1234 --model local_stub`
- To inspect failing cases: `jq .cases[] | select(.metrics.primary < 0.8)` on the artifact jsonl
- To get exact prompt + model request body: artifacts include request_trace.jsonl with fields {case_id, request, response, latency_ms}.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to standardize embedding computation across teams (library + version pin) to keep semantic-sim comparisons consistent? (proposal: use `redwood-embed==0.9.1` binary artifact in wheel cache)
- We should add a tiny Rust shim for the tokenizer normalization step to make exact-match deterministic across languages. Cost/benefit TBD.
- Decide whether nightly runs should re-evaluate using the latest prompt-manifest or freeze the prompt-manifest used during the model training. (Lean: freeze per-run for auditability.)

Appendix: quick GH Actions snippet (to copy):
name: evals-smoke
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: restore pip cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('**/requirements.txt') }}
      - name: run smoke evals
        run: |
          python ci/run_smoke.py --seed $(( ${{ github.sha }} | fold -w2 | head -n1 | xxd -r -p ) 2>/dev/null || echo 1234)

---

If people want, I can split this into an actual starter repo with templates for the runner scaffold and GH workflows (saves time for new model onboarding). For now: please comment on the gating thresholds and whether we want embedding-based scores in PR smoke (probably not: keep PR light).

Notes to self: follow up with Marco on loader validation shim; Renee to draft metrics-config schema.
